ai-at-work.title: Anthropic’s prospectus details losses, growth, and, yes, a warning that its AI could end humanity
ai-at-work.excerpt: In its prospectus, Anthropic just told investors it's losing tens of billions of dollars a year, but also growing like crazy, and — oh yeah — its own AI might pose an existential risk to humanity.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic disclosed in its IPO filing that it's hemorrhaging billions annually while scaling aggressively, plus casually mentioned that its AI could theoretically pose an existential threat to humanity. This matters because digital workplace leaders are actively deploying AI tools into their environments right now, and if the company building some of these systems is genuinely worried about existential risk, that's worth factoring into your vendor risk assessment. Apparently the business model is "move fast and break things, or possibly break civilization," which is a bold strategy for a company asking people to trust it with their enterprise data.

ai-at-work.title: The AI boom took over Climate Week and not everyone is happy about it
ai-at-work.excerpt: Just like the rest of the U.S., data centers and AI are dividing climate tech founders and investors.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: AI dominated Climate Week conversations this year, with data centers and AI infrastructure becoming central to climate tech discussions. Digital workplace leaders need to pay attention because this tension directly affects where enterprise tech investment flows and what infrastructure decisions get made around their tools and platforms. Here's the thing though: if you're still debating whether AI belongs at a climate conference in 2024, you've already missed the plot. The real conversation should be about building efficient systems, not pretending the technology doesn't exist.

ai-at-work.title: Nvidia launches new platform for reining in rogue AI agents
ai-at-work.excerpt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Monday introduced a toolkit of software and hardware products that add independent security layers around AI agents to ensure they stay within their test environments even i
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Nvidia just released security tools designed to keep AI agents from going rogue and escaping their sandboxes, giving enterprises actual guardrails for their AI experiments. This matters because companies deploying AI agents in production are rightfully paranoid about uncontrolled behavior, and having vendor-backed containment options beats crossing your fingers and hoping for the best. Honestly, it's refreshing to see someone building fences before we need them, though I'd still trust but verify whatever Nvidia's definition of "contained" actually means in practice.

ai-at-work.title: Anthropic releases Sonnet 5.5, which it calls a significantly cheaper, faster work partner
ai-at-work.excerpt: Anthropic has released the newest version of its mid-range model, boasting faster response times and less token burn.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic rolled out Sonnet 5.5, a faster and cheaper version of their mid-range Claude model that burns through fewer tokens. This matters because most workplace teams using Claude for content creation, analysis, and automation will suddenly get more bang for their buck, which means your AI budget might actually stretch further next year. Of course, the real test is whether it's actually faster in real work or just faster at telling you it's faster, so run your own tests before you bet the farm on it.

tools-tech.title: Try Google Drive Projects for fast, focused AI analysis
tools-tech.excerpt: Google Drive is the cloud platform for storing and organizing your Google Workspace files: documents, presentations, spreadsheets, and even media (images, audio, and video). If your Workspace account
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google added AI-powered project analysis capabilities to Google Drive, letting Workspace users with Gemini access prompt the AI to analyze and summarize their stored files directly within the platform. This matters because it reduces friction for knowledge workers who live in Drive and need quick insights without switching tools or copying content elsewhere. Here's the thing though: if your organization hasn't figured out its Gemini governance yet, you're about to have some very creative employees feeding proprietary data to Google's AI in ways your security team didn't anticipate.

digital-culture.title: How to reclaim your ambition
digital-culture.excerpt: Recent news stories have suggested that younger workers are opting out of work ambition. Coverage documents their frustration with a limiting job market, dehumanizing hiring processes, and the expecta
digital-culture.dwp_take: Younger workers are scaling back career ambition due to real frustrations with hiring practices and hustle culture, but the media's relentless negative messaging is making things worse. Digital workplace leaders need to understand this distinction because blaming "lazy Gen Z" misses the actual design problems in how we recruit, onboard, and treat people. Here's the truth: if your workplace can't attract ambitious talent, the problem is probably your workplace, not the generation.

digital-culture.title: How to onboard a virtual teammate
digital-culture.excerpt: Imagine going to a job board, making a hire for a chief of staff, and onboarding that new hire within a few minutes. That’s the fantasy that artificial intelligence companies are making a reality with
digital-culture.dwp_take: Optimizely released AI "virtual teammates" that can supposedly get up to speed and productive in minutes, positioning them as ready-to-work role-specific AI coworkers. This matters because it signals a real shift in how companies think about filling capability gaps, and digital workplace leaders need to understand these tools are now competing for budget that used to go to training programs and junior hires. Here's the thing though: I've watched a lot of "ready in minutes" solutions over three decades, and onboarding is never actually the hard part. Making someone actually useful on your team is.

digital-culture.title: eBay’s CEO finds ideas through constant feedback
digital-culture.excerpt: Hello and welcome to Modern CEO! I’m Stephanie Mehta, CEO and chief content officer of Mansueto Ventures. Each week this newsletter explores inclusive approaches to leadership drawn from conversations
digital-culture.dwp_take: eBay's CEO apparently runs regular feedback loops with employees to surface ideas and stay connected to what's actually happening on the ground. This matters because it's a reminder that the tools and platforms we build in digital workplaces only work if leaders actually use them to listen instead of just broadcast. The irony is that most companies have enterprise feedback systems gathering dust while their leaders still make decisions in information vacuums, so good on Jamie Iannone for doing the obvious thing.

digital-culture.title: Meta-Led Anti-Terrorism Group Faces Mass Resignation of Expert Advisers
digital-culture.excerpt: Meta and other tech giants are pushing through structural changes at the Global Internet Forum to Counter Terrorism that outside researchers allege will weaken oversight of an already embattled consor
digital-culture.dwp_take: Meta and its tech giant peers are restructuring the Global Internet Forum to Counter Terrorism in ways that researchers say will reduce independent oversight of their content moderation efforts. This matters because digital workplace leaders depend on these forums to understand how platforms handle misinformation and extremism, especially when employees are working across those same tools. When the people watching the watchers start heading for the exits, it's usually not because they think things are heading in the right direction.

industry-news.excerpt: Nvidia adds a Sentry hardware monitoring design to its AI agent safety platform. See what OpenShell offers now and what IT teams still need to verify. The post Nvidia Adds Hardware Monitoring Design t
industry-news.dwp_take: Nvidia just bolted hardware monitoring capabilities onto its AI agent safety platform, basically giving your systems a security guard that watches the machine itself, not just the software. For digital workplace teams, this matters because AI agents are moving into production environments fast, and you need visibility into whether they're doing what you actually asked them to do or just making expensive mistakes on your infrastructure. The irony is that we've spent thirty years trying to get business users to monitor their own behavior, and now we have to babysit the AI doing their jobs.

industry-news.excerpt: Truecaller Scam Checker lets users check suspicious links, numbers, and messages for free as the company expands its fraud protection beyond caller ID. The post Truecaller Scam Checker Launches in Ind
industry-news.dwp_take: Truecaller launched a new Scam Checker feature in India that lets users verify suspicious links, phone numbers, and messages at no cost, expanding beyond their traditional caller ID blocking. This matters because digital workplace security is only as strong as employee awareness, and tools that help staff spot phishing attempts and fraud reduce breach risk at the source. Here's the thing though: a scam checker is just a band aid if your organization hasn't trained people to think critically about what they're clicking in the first place.
